statements.reading: Stated as an outcome of the framework. In words it matches #11 App. A item 4 (dark matter is conjugate matter). What 'dual' means is fixed in §2: the metastring dual coordinate (statements below).

statements.quote: In this paper we consider the inclusion of the dual matter which, to first order in \lambda , can be interpreted as the dark matter as well as providing an intrinsic stringy resolution to the hierarchy problem.
statements.reading: Presented as this paper's step ('In this paper we consider') and as an interpretation ('can be interpreted as'), at first order in λ: a proposal, not a derivation.

statements.quote: Furthermore in this new approach, the known Standard Model fields and their dark matter duals are dynamically correlated, and we comment on various phenomenological signatures stemming from this correlation.
statements.reading: Each SM field has a dark dual, and the two are correlated by the dynamics. In #11 P4 the sectors share only gravity.

statements.reading: x̃ is the left-minus-right zero mode: the T-dual, winding-type coordinate. Eq. (3) gives [x̂^a, x̃̂_b] = 2πiλ²δ^a_b and [x̂^a, x̂^b] = 0 = [x̃̂_a, x̃̂_b]. The particle action (13), p ẋ + p̃ x̃̇ − λ² p ṗ̃, carries a separate momentum p̃ for x̃. So x̃ is conjugate to x at λ² = α′, not the momentum p at ℏ (my reading). #11 places χ in the p-polarization of one phase space (x, p), with ω rigid (P2′, P4).

'Canonically conjugate' is said here of the x̃ of eq. statements.reading: The paper calls it 'the proposal'. It names the first channel of correlation: through the dark-energy sector. [18] is the modified-dark-matter (MDM) papers of Ho, Minic, Ng, Edmonds, Farrah and Takeuchi, 2010–2020. #11 has no such channel.

statements.quote: In this section we elaborate on the dual matter degrees of freedom and the explicit appearance of dark matter in the general formulation of string theory [14].
statements.reading: Credits the appearance of dark matter to [14]: the Freidel–Leigh–Minic papers of 2014–2019 and Minic arXiv:2003.00318. In my search, the arXiv papers of [14] contain no 'dark matter' (see Q11).

statements.quote: For concreteness, let us start with a vector background, by shifting the momenta and the dual momenta by the standard, minimally coupled gauge field and its dual [14]:
statements.reading: Dual fields enter as background fields of the dual momentum: p → p + A(x,x̃), p̃ → p̃ + Ã(x,x̃). A dark field is the gauge field that couples to p̃, the momentum of x̃. It is not matter localized in the momentum of x (my reading).

statements.quote: These gauge fields have the usual Abelian gauge symmetries.
statements.reading: The dual gauge field has a gauge invariance of its own: a separate dual photon. No magnetic charge of our photon is mentioned. Compare #11 §11.4's separate-photon form (my comparison).

statements.quote: In other words, in the observable spacetime, the visible sector and its dual/dark counterpart are “mixed/correlated” (19), in a way that is sensitive to both the UV and IR cutoffs. statements.reading: Through λ⁸/L¹⁰⟦φ,φ̃⟧, which the paper calls 'an explicit correlation between the dark matter sector and a visible sector'.

statements.reading: Predicts a dual photon correlated with ours, the correlation dominating ordinary kinetic mixing. #11 §13 row 7 names 'Any confirmed non-gravitational DM–SM coupling' as what kills the program's candidates; this is such a coupling (my inference).

statements.quote: These type of correlations might be found in correlated events in the accelerators, but which are not products of any standard particle decays.

statements.reading: The sentence says L may lie 'within one or two orders of magnitude' of λ. My computation (scratch/r2-dual-sm/scripts/mixing_scale.py) gives the suppression (λ/L)¹⁰ = 1.0e-10 at L/λ = 10 and 1.0e-20 at L/λ = 100, relative to the fundamental scale. statements.quote: Finally, we note that the peculiar correlation between the visible and dark sectors, discussed for scalar, pseudo-scalar, fermionic and vector degrees of freedom, can be also found in the gravitational and dual gravitational sectors.

statements.reading: In the semiclassical extensification where holography emerges, the dual degrees of freedom decouple completely: a second limit in which the dual sector disappears.

statements.quote: This new view of string theory should bring about a different viewpoint on the vacuum selection problem (along the lines of the attractor solutions found in [53]), as well as the selection of a robust quantum matter sector which is mutually consistent with the quantum gravitational sector and their respective duals.
statements.reading: Vacuum selection is named as an open problem, with an analogy to attractor solutions ([53] is a paper on genetic-code evolution). No mechanism, potential or order parameter. #11 P2′/P5 read the selection as spontaneous, with η as order parameter.

papers.summary: The first refereed statement of the identification, posted 29 Oct 2020. Every metastring field φ(x,x̃) has a dual φ̃(x,x̃), and the duals of the SM fields are proposed as dark matter. The dark sector is tied to ours two ways: through the dark-energy sector (MDM), and through mixing terms from the symplectic term λ² p ṗ̃ (vector and scalar λ⁸/L¹⁰, fermion mass mixing λ⁹/L¹⁰ with seesaw relations), plus an FF̃ term in the doubled action. The mixing is invisible to EFT and vanishes as λ → 0 or L → ∞. It can be finite under a double scaling, and is called phenomenologically realistic for L within 1–2 orders of λ. The paper predicts a dual photon correlated with ours, a dual Z, dual-QCD effects in the deep IR and correlated accelerator events. Here x̃ is the left-minus-right zero mode, with [x,x̃] = 2πiλ² and its own momentum p̃. The size of the dual space sets G_N and its curvature gives Λ > 0. There are no monopoles, no velocity dependence and no spontaneous selection of the polarization.

papers.summary: A talk by Minic at MG16, whose text overlaps substantially with Minic 2020. It shows both meanings of x̃. In the modular-spacetime foundations, x̃ = p/ε with λε = ℏ, the canonical conjugate at ℏ. In the metastring and the metaparticle, X = (x, x̃) has separate momenta (p, p̃), with [X,P] = iℏ and [X,X] = 2πiλ²ω at the string length. Gauging p̃ gives a dual field Ã 'correlated (entangled)' with A, and 'the entire SM would have a dual SM (which we propose, describes the dark matter sector)'. Dark quanta 'should be detectable' through Berry-phase-like correlation. If MDM quanta are metaparticles, that 'may explain' the null results. Observational hooks: an acceleration scale ~cH₀ in the BTF and BFJ relations, and a predicted (1+z) scaling of σ⁴/(GM_bar). Dark matter is assumed collisionless in the turbulence analogy. The polarization is a choice, ambiguous up to T-duality.

papers.summary: Five pages. Polarizing the doubled metastring space on one half rather than the other swaps the tangent and cotangent bundles, which the authors read as mirror symmetry. In a re-bosonized heterotic Ansatz, η pairs the roots of E8 (on x) and Ẽ8 (on x̃), 'which identifies Ẽ8 as the Langlands dual, E∨8, i.e., the electro-magnetic dual'; the two are 'physically indistinguishable'. Each gauge field has a 'dark' dual in the same algebra, and a λ₄²/L⁴ term correlates the visible E8 fields with the dark Ẽ8 fields. The paper treats gauge groups only: no matter, no charges, no monopoles, and no explicit dark-matter claim.

papers.summary: A 118-page review that restates and extends 2010.15610. §4.3: each particle has a dual particle, a good dark-matter candidate correlated with visible matter. Metaparticle interactions conserve p and p̃, with a static Friedel-form potential. Dual degrees of freedom dominate early and freeze late, and the detection analysis should be revisited. §4.4: the polarization 'is not fixed'; picking x or the dual polarization gives the same result. §4.9: two Heisenberg algebras, [x,p] = i and [x,x̃] = il_s². §6.1: x̃ is the winding coordinate, λ not the 4d Planck length. §6.4: dual fields are 'canonically conjugate' to SM fields and do not commute with them. The 4d mixing is λ₄²/L⁴ for vectors, scalars and axions and λ₄³/L⁴ for fermion masses, with λ₄ and L unspecified and the terms vanishing as λ₄ → 0 or L → ∞. The review adds a dual SM, a dual Higgs and a dual neutrino, and light dual states as dark radiation. §6.5: a dual photon and dual Z, accelerator events, a mass gap that 'may well be phenomenologically relevant', and the dual Higgs as an inflaton. §6.6: Ẽ8 is the electric–magnetic (Langlands) dual; 'their dual “dark” Ẽ8-fields'; Born geometry 'also involves S-duality'. §7: Λ from the dual curvature and G_N from the dual size; quintessence 'rather unnatural'.

answers.question: Q1 Identification
answers.answer: Yes. All five dark-matter papers state it (2109.01122 has no dark-matter content), with varying firmness. Abstracts and conclusions state it as an outcome: 'dark matter ... comes from the degrees of freedom dual to the visible matter' (2010.15610 abstract, §8), a 'new understanding of dark matter in terms of metaparticles' (2109.12763 abstract), 'The dark matter degrees of freedom are thus tied to the dual particles to the visible SM particles' (2307.16712 §5). The body frames it as a proposal or candidacy: 'can be interpreted as' (2010.15610 §1), 'The proposal here is that the dual sector ... should be interpreted as the dark matter sector' (2010.15610 §3, 2109.12763 §5, 2212.06086 §6.3), 'which we propose' (2109.12763 §4), 'good candidates' (2212.06086 §4.3), 'a candidate dark matter companion' (2307.16712 §3). No paper derives it; the only observational support offered is MDM's fits. The closest wording to C1 is 2212.06086 §6.4: 'the dual particles are conjugate to the Standard Model particles in analogy with the canonical fact that momenta p are conjugate to coordinates q', glossed as the dual fields not commuting with SM fields. That is field-space conjugacy of each field with its dual, a different relation from #11 P4's separate p-polarized species (my reading).

answers.question: Q2 What 'dual' is
answers.answer: These papers use x̃ in two senses. (a) In the modular-spacetime foundations x̃ is the momentum: x̂ ≡ q̂/λ, x̃̂ ≡ p̂/ε with λε = ℏ, so [x̂, x̃̂] = i (2109.12763 §2), and p → εx̃ in the phase-space count (2307.16712 §2.2). That is the canonical conjugate at ℏ, the program's sense. (b) In the metastring and metaparticle, which the dark-matter statements are built on, x̃ is the left-minus-right zero mode, 'the dual (winding) coordinates' (2212.06086 §6.1; 2010.15610 §2; 2111.14205; 2307.16712 eq. 2.45). There [x̂^a, x̃̂_b] = 2πiλ²δ^a_b and [x,x] = 0 = [x̃,x̃] at B = 0 (2010.15610 eq. 3; 2109.12763 eq. 14; 2212.06086 eqs. 6.1, 6.5), or iℓ_s² (2212.06086 §4.9; 2307.16712 eq. 3.1). x̃ has its own momentum: [X, P] = iℏ (2109.12763 §3.1), [X, Π] = iℏ = [X̃, Π̃] (2307.16712 eq. 3.2), [p, p̃] = 0 (2307.16712 §2.4), and the Poisson bracket {x̃, x} = πα′ (2212.06086 eq. 4.19). 2212.06086 §4.9 says outright that 'the metastring is endowed with two Heisenberg algebras', [x,p] = i and [x,x̃] = il_s². It calls the doubled space a phase space 'since the metastring action requires ... a background symplectic form' (§4.3). The scale of [x, x̃] varies: λ 'such as the fundamental Planck scale' (2010.15610 §2); λ ∼ (M_P^(10))⁻¹ ≲ 10⁻¹⁹ m, 'not to be confused with' the 4d Planck length (2212.06086 fn 38; my computation: ħc/λ = 1.97 TeV); a minimal length bound of O(10 TeV) (2109.12763 §3.1); ℓ_nc 'in principle contextual, and not necessarily the string length or the Planck length' (2307.16712 §4.1). The dual phase space is assumed Planck-sized (2212.06086 §4.9; 2307.16712 §3). The school also glosses x̃ as the 'long-distance (IR)' spacetime (2212.06086 §6.1) and the 'dual (momentum-like) spacetime' (2307.16712 §4.1). Dark fields Ã enter by minimally coupling the dual momentum p̃ (2010.15610 eq. 14; 2109.12763 §2.2). So in the dark-matter model x̃ is an independent T-dual coordinate, not the momentum of x. #11 places χ in the other polarization of one phase space (x, p), with ω rigid at ℏ (P2′, P4, P5).

answers.question: Q3 Field content
answers.answer: Yes: one dual per field. 'For every φ(x,x̃) there exists a dual φ̃(x,x̃)' (2010.15610 §3; 2212.06086 §6.3). 'The entire SM would have a dual SM' (2109.12763 §4), and 'every Standard Model field φ(x) is doubled' (2307.16712 §2.4). Named partners: a dual photon 'distinct from the dark photon of effective field theory', a dual Z distinct from a Z′, dual QCD (2010.15610 §5; 2212.06086 §6.5); a dual neutrino and dual Higgs, the latter a possible Starobinsky-like inflaton (2212.06086 §6.4–§6.5); a dual axion (§6.4); a dual gravity sector R̃(x̃) that gives dark energy (§4.3). Dual gauge fields 'have the usual Abelian gauge symmetries' (2010.15610 §4), so the dual photon is a separate gauge field (my reading; compare #11 §11.4's separate-photon form). Dual charges are not addressed. In the heterotic setting each E8 gauge field has a 'dark' dual in the same algebra (2111.14205; 2212.06086 §6.6), and the dark sector's dual SM comes 'from the other E8' (2307.16712 §4.3). There is also a kinematic dual: 'for each particle at energy E there exists a dual particle at energy μ/E' (2109.12763 §4), and metaparticles are 'correlated pairs of particles and their duals' (2307.16712 §3). The one-dual-per-field structure parallels #11 §11.4's one magnetic analog per charged particle, without magnetic charges (my comparison). #11 §12 itself names three candidates, not a dual SM.

answers.question: Q4 Coupling
answers.answer: The papers state four channels besides gravity. (1) Through dark energy: the dual sector 'is correlated to the visible sector via the dark energy sector', citing MDM (2010.15610 §3; 2109.12763 §5; 2212.06086 §6.3). (2) Bilinear mixing terms. These come from the symplectic term λ² p ṗ̃ of the metaparticle action once p → p + A and p̃ → p̃ + Ã. In the doubled space: ∫[F² − aλ²⟦A,Ã⟧ + F̃² + FF̃ + …] (2010.15610 eq. 15; 2212.06086 eq. 6.27, 'clearly not present in the usual effective field theory approach'). In x-space after integrating x̃, 2010.15610 has vector −(λ⁸/L¹⁰) f⟦A,Ã⟧, scalar λ⁸/L¹⁰ and fermion λ⁹/L¹⁰ ψ̄ψ̃ (eqs. 19–21). 2212.06086 rewrites these in 4d as λ₄²/L⁴ times dimensionless 'Berry phase-like background fluxes', and λ₄³/L⁴ for fermions (eqs. 6.32–6.35). The fermion term is 'quite explicitly a mass-mixing term': each fermion and its dual share a mass matrix [[m, λ⁹/L¹⁰],[λ⁹/L¹⁰, m̃]], with seesaw relations and possibly neutrino masses (2010.15610 §5; 2212.06086 eq. 6.36). 2212.06086 §6.6 adds gauge–gravity terms. The dual photon's correlation is 'finite even in the limit of zero momenta' and dominates ordinary dark-photon mixing (2010.15610 §5). (3) Entanglement: the metaparticle 'looks like two particles that are entangled through a Berry-phase-like p ṗ̃ factor' (2109.12763 §4). This is what 'correlated (entangled)' means. Strength is not fixed. 2010.15610 §6 calls λ an effective scale 'to be empirically determined', and 2212.06086 fn 43 leaves λ₄ and L 'unspecified'. 2010.15610 §6 lets L lie 'within one or two orders of magnitude' of λ, 'resulting in a phenomenologically realistic scale'. 2212.06086 §6.5 says the mass gap 'may well be phenomenologically relevant', the details being 'model-dependent'. answers.question: Q5 Detection
answers.answer: Colliders: 'correlated events in the accelerators, ... not products of any standard particle decays'; a dual photon correlated with ours and distinct from the EFT dark photon; a dual Z distinct from a Z′; dual-QCD effects in the deep IR (2010.15610 §5; 2212.06086 §6.5). Particle physics: neutrino masses through the dual-neutrino seesaw (2010.15610 §4–§5; 2212.06086 §6.4–§6.5); a new view of the strong-CP problem by averaging over a constant axion (both); CP phases from the dual SM (2307.16712 §4.3); the dual Higgs as an inflaton (2212.06086 §6.5); a deformed dispersion relation E² + μ²/E² = p² + m², with a neutrino bound putting μ near the dark-energy scale (2109.12763 §4; 2212.06086 §4.3, citing arXiv:2104.00802). Astrophysics and cosmology: MDM's acceleration scale cH₀ ~ 10⁻¹⁰ m/s² in galaxy and cluster fits and in the BTF and BFJ relations; a predicted (1+z) scaling of σ⁴/(GM_bar) (2109.12763 §6). The authors caveat that BFJ 'could well be explained by more conventional means' and that MDM lacks 'concrete scenarios'. Also: the H0 tension, through dual gravity (2010.15610 §4), a varying G_N (2212.06086 §6.2) or light dual states as dark radiation (§6.4); the coincidence of dark and visible abundances (2212.06086 §4.8; 2307.16712 §5); 'one should search for metaparticles' (2212.06086 §7). Direct detection: dark quanta 'should be detectable through their particular metaparticle correlation/entanglement' (2109.12763 §4). 'If the quanta of MDM are metaparticles, this may explain why, so far, dark matter detection experiments have failed' (2109.12763 §6.1): conditional, with no mechanism given. The 'usual detection analysis ... should be revisited' (2212.06086 §4.3). No paper predicts a permanent null. My inference: the school's collider and dual-photon signals are non-gravitational DM–SM couplings, which #11 §13 row 7 names as killing the program's candidates. A confirmed signal of that kind would therefore separate the two, which bears on the open question in root CLAUDE.md. The MDM acceleration-scale correlation is likewise a halo prediction the program does not make (#11 §13 row 1 is a knee in σ_T(v)).

answers.question: Q6 Gravity
answers.answer: Newton's constant is set by the size of the dual space and Λ by its curvature. Integrating x̃ in Tseytlin's ∫∫√g√g̃[R(x) + R̃(x̃)] 'defines the gravitational constant G_N' (2010.15610 §2; 2109.12763 §5). 'The size of the dual space is the gravitational constant' (2212.06086 §7). 'G_N could vary by varying the volume of the dual spacetime' (2212.06086 §6.2). With Ṽ ∼ V⁻¹ by T-duality the action becomes intensive (2109.12763 §5). Dark matter gravitates on the observed metric: after x̃-integration, L̃_dm(x) sits beside L_m(x) under √−g(x) (2010.15610 eq. 8; 2109.12763 eqs. 24, 32; 2212.06086 eq. 6.19). There is also a dual gravity sector R̃(x̃), 'associated with a dynamical dual spacetime', which gives dark energy (2212.06086 §4.3). It is correlated with ours 'via the scale of non-commutativity' (2010.15610 §4; 2212.06086 §6.4). Compare #11 §8, where χ propagates on g, and §7, where momentum gravity is a massive spin-2 X. The school has no massive dual graviton; its dual gravity is the dual curvature (my comparison).

answers.question: Q7 Dynamics
answers.answer: Mostly not addressed. Interactions are set aside: 'we will not consider metaparticle interactions directly in this paper, such interactions preserve both p and p̃'. A static potential of 'Friedel form' e^{−αr}/r^β cos(γr) is cited as unpublished work (2212.06086 §4.3 fn 31). There is no velocity dependence, no gate in relative momentum and no overlap of momenta (compare #11 §8). 2109.12763 §6.2 takes dark matter as collisionless, 'whether traditional or metaparticle', for its turbulence analogy. p̃ acts as Lorentz-transforming 'internal' quantum numbers of a state (2212.06086 §4.3). A dual particle has energy μ/E (2109.12763 §4). The dual degrees of freedom dominate in the early universe and are 'frozen' in a large, old one (2212.06086 §4.3, §5.3, citing arXiv:2104.00802). No localization in x̃ or in momentum, no condensate and no wave or fuzzy form appears.

answers.question: Q8 Monopoles
answers.answer: No paper has magnetically charged or dyonic objects, as dark matter or otherwise. None places anything magnetic in x̃ or in momentum. What appears is electric–magnetic duality of gauge groups and S-duality remarks. In the heterotic Ansatz, η makes the roots of Ẽ8 (on x̃) 'reciprocal' to those of E8 (on x), 'which identifies Ẽ8 as the Langlands dual, E∨8, i.e., the electro-magnetic dual'. The two are 'physically indistinguishable' because E8 is simply laced (2111.14205; 2212.06086 §6.6). Visible E8 fields correlate with 'dark' Ẽ8 fields. 2212.06086 calls these 'their dual “dark” Ẽ8-fields' and adds that Born geometry 'also involves S-duality'. Its fn 24 says S-duality patching 'requires re-incorporating winding modes and “momentum” space'. 2307.16712 puts the dark sector's dual SM in 'the other E8' and remarks that 'S-duality must be involved' (fn 11). 2109.12763 §2.2 mentions dual 'electric' and 'magnetic' variables of modular QFT. My comparison: these reach #11 §11.3, the charge lattice's polarization and the T/S-duality bridge (flag 67), and resemble #14 v2's 'S-dual image' reading of the momentum-polarized sector. They contain no monopole and nothing localized in momentum.

answers.question: Q9 Polarization and vacuum
answers.answer: The polarization is a choice, with no mechanism. 'A choice of polarization is a choice of a spacetime' (2109.12763 §2.1). 'The spacetime polarization is not fixed. Still one can pick a particular ... spacetime polarization'; 'we could have picked the dual, x̃,p polarization', with the same seesaw 'in either case' (2212.06086 §4.4). The spacetime is 'ambiguous, with different choices related by ... T-duality' (2109.12763 §4; 2212.06086 §4.3; 2307.16712 §2.4). Polarizing on the complementary half swaps T and T*, which the authors read as mirror symmetry (2111.14205; 2212.06086 §6.6). The section condition is likened to choosing the coordinate or momentum representation, 'or indeed any other (αp+βq)-polarization' (2111.14205). The other choice is thus treated as related by a symmetry and equally valid, which bears on #11 P5's 'mirror vacuum is equally lawful' (my reading). No potential or order parameter selects the polarization. H relates to 'the choice of quantum vacuum' (2212.06086 §6.1) and the vacuum depends on H (2109.12763 §2.1); η, H and ω are dynamical fields. 'Vacuum selection' is named only as a problem to be seen anew, 'along the lines of the attractor solutions' (2010.15610 §8). The one spontaneous breaking in these papers is of the second Lorentz group O(1,d−1)₂ in a sector of fixed p̃ (2212.06086 §4.3), not of Born duality. This is consistent with #11 §3, which credits the preferred polarization to Freidel, Leigh and Minic and claims only the spontaneous reading.

answers.question: Q10 Dark energy
answers.answer: Dark energy is a positive cosmological constant from the curvature of the dual spacetime. 'The curvature of the dual space is the cosmological constant in the observed spacetime' (2212.06086 §7; 2010.15610 §2; 2109.12763 §5; 2307.16712 §5), with a seesaw M_Λ M_P ∼ M_H². The equation of state is 'p = −ρ' (2212.06086 §5.3), so w = −1. Quintessence alternatives appear 'rather unnatural' (2212.06086 §7) and 'tend to induce too low a value for the Hubble constant' (§2). Two pointers go to dynamical dark energy: 'a dynamical form of dark energy [51]' (2109.12763 §5) and 'predictive power ... in particular the equation of state for the dark energy' ([285], 2212.06086 §4.8). Neither paper gives a w. 2109.01122 gives a positive Λ on a de Sitter bubble-world, also w = −1. Against #11 §10: the school's main line is a constant Λ, where the program's τ is thawing quintessence with w ≥ −1. Both lines would come under pressure from w ≠ −1 data, in different directions (my comparison). The school maps the dual space's curvature to our Λ; #11 §10's corrected dictionary maps dual curvature to negative dark radiation and dual stiff matter to Λ. The two constructions differ: Tseytlin's intensive action with Ṽ ∼ V⁻¹, against a shared lapse with a·ã = 1 (my comparison). On C5 ('Their collapse is our acceleration', App. A item 9): nothing in these papers has the dual spacetime contract or collapse. It is static and Planck-sized ('the big spacetime is balanced by a Planckian dual spacetime, and vice versa', 2212.06086 §4.4). Its degrees of freedom dominate early and freeze late (2212.06086 §4.3, §5.3), and Ṽ ∼ V⁻¹ (2109.12763 §5) parallels a·ã = 1 (App. A item 6). The acceleration comes from the dual curvature, not from a collapse.

answers.question: Q11 Priority
answers.answer: My six papers all postdate Minic 2020 (29 Feb 2020; not among my papers). The earliest of them is 2010.15610, v1 posted 29 Oct 2020; I checked its v1 PDF, which holds the identification, the correlation and the dual photon. 2010.15610 presents the identification as its own step ('In this paper we consider'). I ran tools/lit.py text with --grep on seven arXiv papers of the series: 1307.7080, 1405.3949, 1502.08005, 1606.01829, 1706.03305, 1707.00312 and 1812.10821 ('Theory of metaparticles'). Each gave 0 matches for 'dark matter' and 0 for 'dark sector|dark energy', so these citations are to the formalism. The 2019 Berglund–Hübsch–Minic papers 1905.08269 and 1905.09463 mention dark matter only as a pointer to MDM. Ho–Minic–Ng 2010–2011 (abstracts only) propose 'a duality between cold dark matter and modified Newtonian dynamics': a different duality. No statement outside the school is cited. Unread: Freidel–Leigh–Minic IJMPA 34 (2019) 1941004 (not on arXiv; its abstract mentions metaparticles but not dark matter) and J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 804 (2017) 012032 (IOP bot check). Within what I could read, Minic 2020 stays the earliest statement, as the record says.
